Tuition coverage to check

The advertised package covers Home-rate tuition. It should not be treated as full international-fee funding: confirm your fee status and any overseas-fee difference with the university before accepting.

About the Research

Long-distance quantum communication faces a major technical problem: photons are gradually lost as they travel through optical fibre. Quantum repeaters are being developed as a possible way of extending quantum communication over much greater distances. This Manchester project will investigate a hybrid system combining III-V semiconductor quantum-dot photon sources and warm rubidium atomic vapour. The goal is to develop interfaces capable of frequency conversion and subsequent storage of photons in rubidium vapour.

Research Activities

The successful student is expected to work across areas including: quantum-dot photon sources; rubidium atomic vapour; frequency conversion; photon storage; quantum optics; semiconductor physics; atomic physics; cryogenic optical measurements; optical system design; electromagnetically induced transparency; four-wave mixing; numerical modelling; and quantum networking. The student will work with collaborators in the UK and internationally. Part of the research is connected to Manchester work on testing quantum telecommunications over metropolitan communication links.

Funding

The studentship is funded for 3.5 years. The successful student receives £21,805 per year tax-free stipend at the 2026/27 UKRI rate, tuition-fee coverage, and annual stipend increases where UKRI rates rise. The current advertisement specifies that the funding is available to candidates eligible for Home tuition-fee status. This means international applicants who are classified as Overseas-fee students should not assume that full international tuition fees will be covered.

Eligibility

Applicants should normally have or expect to receive: at least a UK 2:1 honours degree; a relevant master's degree; or an international equivalent, in a suitable science or engineering discipline. Relevant backgrounds may include: physics; quantum technology; electrical/electronic engineering; photonics; optical engineering; materials science; or closely related areas.

Supervisor

Dr Joanna Zajac is a Lecturer in Quantum Technology in Manchester's Photon Physics Group. Her official Manchester profile lists research interests including: III-V quantum dots; neutral atoms; quantum repeaters; telecom devices; and quantum sensing. Her university profile also confirms that she is currently accepting PhD students.

Contact

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official announcement page (see the Official Link section above). Always quote the position reference in your message so the admissions or HR team can route your enquiry quickly.

Official Link

Full announcement and application portal: https://research.manchester.ac.uk/en/persons/joanna-zajac/

Source: research.manchester.ac.uk - the details in this listing were recorded from this official page.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: 1 December 2026 - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official portal before the deadline: 1 December 2026. Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents — early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.
